thread:
Anya V: quick sync — proposal for per-route debug_token + sampling + redaction flow. want to avoid leaking PII to SRE while keeping fast debug for prod issues. thoughts?
Jordan P: +1 need this. main constraints: latency SLOs, quota accounting, and audit trail for any unredacted access.
Phil K: can we make it opt-in per-tenant with TTL? e.g., debug_token valid for 1h and records flagged as 'ephemeral-inspect' rather than normal logs.
Anya V: yep — tenant-scoped, expire, and must require breakglass role to mint. For routing: route to debug workers behind dedicated capacity so we don't affect normal throughput.
Maria S: question: what do we store in telemetry when debug_token used? full payload retained? partial? we have legal/compliance concerns.
LegalBot: (automated) anything tagged ephemeral-inspect must be logged in audit with user, token_id, reason, and expiration. Full request/response may be retained only if explicit consent or enterprise contract.
Jordan P: proposal: two-tier retention. 1) default telemetry: scrubbed request/response with redaction metadata header. 2) ephemeral full capture: encrypted, short TTL, access only via audit-approved flow.
Phil K: how to represent redaction in headers so downstream services know not to persist? idea:
```
X-Redwood-Inspect: token=abcd1234; mode=ephemeral; redacted=true; fields=client_email,credit_card
```
This lets console and services show why fields omitted.
Anya V: +1. Also add a hash of the user id so sampling can be deterministic but still pseudonymous: `uid_hash=sha256(user_id + tenant_salt)` so we can roll up metrics without raw ids.
Maria S: sampling strategy debate: deterministic sampling on uid_hash vs random sampling on route. Deterministic avoids user-hotness skew. But it means some users always sampled. legal: is that ok?
LegalBot: deterministic sampling is acceptable if hashes are irreversible and salts managed. Must document salt rotation policy and revoke old salts on breach.
Jordan P: operational concerns: if many tenants flip debug, we may blow quota. Suggest quota-aware routing: if debug workers near capacity, fallback to rate-limited scrubbed captures and emit a warning event to tenant.
Phil K: UX: console should show per-route sampling toggle + global breakglass controls. Toggle tooltip: "Ephemeral inspect stores full payload for up to N hours; access requires approval." Also allow per-tenant soft-cap with notification.
Anya V: small API surface sketch:
```
POST /v1/debug-sessions
{ "tenant_id": "t_123", "ttl_mins": 60, "reason": "prod-issue-453", "scopes": ["requests","responses"] }
Response: { "token": "dbg_abc", "expires_at": "2026-03-20T15:04:05Z" }
```
Requests using `Authorization: Bearer dbg_abc` get special routing.
Jordan P: telemetry tag schema:
- debug_mode: ("none","ephemeral","scrubbed")
- redaction_fields: comma list
- inspect_token_id: opaque id
- sampling_rule: "deterministic:user_hash:0.01" or "route:0.1"
Maria S: how do we surface in dashboards? want a column that shows percent of requests with debug_mode != none and breakdown by tenant. Also break out cost impact.
Phil K: security: all ephemeral captures encrypted at rest with tenant-specific KEK. Access via UI requires two-person approval for >30m retention.
Anya V: corner cases: third-party integrators that log request body — we must send a header to inhibit persistence but can't enforce. consider legal notices + customer contract language.
Jordan P: implementation plan: (1) proto headers + routing guards, (2) token minting service + audit entries, (3) console feature flags and quota meter, (4) canary with internal tenants.
Phil K: canary checklist: small preset tenants, metric to watch = p99 latency on normal workers, debug-worker CPU/GPU utilization, unexpected storage growth.
Maria S: timing? I can do console mockups next week. Need API contract for backend to wire.
Anya V: i'll draft RFC doc with header schema, sampling semantics, and legal constraints. aim to start canary in 3 weeks.
Jordan P: one more: add a `redaction_proof` field in telemetry that is a short fingerprint proving we applied canonical redaction rules so auditors can verify without seeing PII.
LegalBot: (automated) recommended: include redaction_proof in audit logs and retain redaction rule version.
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for infra changes — tag #debug-token-routing when ready :rocket:
Phil K: action items: Anya write RFC, Jordan implement token service stub, Maria mock console, I'll design routing fallback. I'll add tasks to eng-platform board.
Anya V: thanks all. Keeping thread here for sync — will ping again when RFC is up. :thumbsup:
